subject: Re: Statera Health — MAP: deployment mode & region decision
messages:
From: Linda King <linda.king@staterahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@staterahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Statera MAP: evaluation plan and hosting options

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really helpful. Attached is a first-pass MAP from our side (Statera-MAP-v1.pdf). Primary asks as we kick off:

- We need to lock hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and region by end of May to meet a Q3 clinical rollout.
- Compliance: HIPAA + regional data residency in the US required; we'll need KMS integration or a private option for certain workloads.
- Timeline: discovery + security review in Apr–May, PoC in mid-May, procurement/contract by Jun.

Questions for you:
1) High-level tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Private — particularly lead times and procurement steps.
2) For Dedicated, what region options and sample cost buckets (estimate) can you provide?
3) Any blockers we should know about re: SOC 2 artifacts or audit evidence?

Attaching the MAP for visibility. Can you and your technical lead sketch an evaluation plan (milestones, owners, timeline) and return by Thursday 4/22 so we can review with procurement?

Thanks,

Linda King
Director of IT Operations
Statera Health
Attachments: Statera-MAP-v1.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Statera MAP: evaluation plan and hosting options

Hi Linda — thanks for the MAP and the clear timeline. Looping in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (account lead).

I've sketched a concise mutual action plan and evaluation checkpoints below (see also attached SOC2-questions.xlsx and dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx):

1) Week of Apr 26 — Discovery + narrow acceptance criteria
   - Owner: Statera tech + Sofia
   - Deliverable: feature gating doc, expected RPS, latency SLOs, data residency matrix

2) May 10–14 — PoC week (hosted + dedicated parity test)
   - Owner: Karthik + Statera DevOps
   - Deliverable: 2 workloads tested (PHI-masked), perf dashboard, cost per 1M tokens

3) May 17 — Decision gate meeting
   - Decision: select Hosted / Dedicated / Private for each workload class
   - Inputs: security signoff, perf results, procurement readiness

4) May 24–Jun 7 — Procurement & contracts (DocuSign links will be shared)

5) Jun 14 — Target for infra provisioning (if Dedicated) / private package kickoff

Proposed default recommendation: run patient-facing low-latency features on Dedicated (US-East) to meet SLOs and use Hosted for non-PHI batch tasks until procurement completes; Private only if FIPS-level KMS or air-gapped is mandatory.

Can you confirm the PoC week and owners by Thursday? We'll update the MAP doc and circulate a HubSpot milestone.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Attachments: SOC2-questions.xlsx, dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Statera MAP: evaluation plan and hosting options

Hi all — quick technical note to help the PoC scope and decision:

- Latency: if your target is 50–150ms p95 for short completion paths we recommend Dedicated with US-East placement (lower network transit from your east-coast clinics).
- Throughput: provide expected concurrent requests and average token lengths; we prepared dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx with three sizing buckets.
- Security: Dedicated supports customer KMS integration (bring-your-own) and isolated GPU pools; Private gives vendor-managed on-prem or VPC with HSM support but adds ~6–10 week lead time for on-prem rollouts.
- Fallbacks: we can land on Hosted with enforced KV/prefix caching and strict retention policies if procurement timing slips — keeps you live with a reduced SLA.

Action items for PoC:
- Statera to provide representative sample payloads + expected concurrency by Fri 4/23
- Redwood (me) will prepare perf harness and ingress endpoints for US-East and US-West

I'll prepare an infra checklist and drop into the shared drive by EOD.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Statera MAP: evaluation plan and hosting options

Linda / team — thanks for the context. A few strategic points as you evaluate: 

- Decision criteria (please confirm at the gate): security (KMS/HSM needs), latency p95, procurement timeline and committed spend, and rollback plan for regressions.
- Commercial: if Statera signs a 12-month Dedicated commit by May 15 we can offer a 60-day service credit and a prioritized provisioning lane.
- Ops: we'll include canary rollout steps to limit blast radius and automated fallback to Hosted variants.

Sofia — please capture the credit and procurement milestones in the MAP doc and include a DocuSign link for the Dedicated SOW. Linda — we'll plan an executive sync the week after PoC if needed.

All — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity. After internal alignment we've decided to proceed with Dedicated for our patient-facing inference (US-East) and Hosted for non-PHI workflows during procurement. Next requests from our side:

- Updated dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx reflecting a 12-month commit and expected RPS ranges (we'll share projected volumes by EOD 4/28).
- Updated MAP with procurement milestones, SOW/DocuSign for Dedicated, and a clear rollback plan.
- Schedule PoC week of May 10 (please confirm availability for Karthik and an ingress endpoint in US-East).

We'll aim to have procurement ready to review by Jun 1. Thanks — looking forward to the PoC.

Best,

Linda King
Director of IT Operations
Statera Health
